Welcome to Dorchester Middle School
It is our pleasure to welcome you to Dorchester Middle School. Our core value is 'Respect'; Respect for each other, Respect for our school, Respect for learning.
Our vision for our school and our community is that we all live the values of ROARS - we are Ready, Original, Ambitious, Respectful and Safe. These values are taught through our curriculum and underpin our behaviour for learning systems.
We are committed to providing education opportunities of the highest quality for all our pupils. We aim to deliver a broad education that is ambitious and stimulating in a caring environment that creates well-rounded individuals who are ready for the challenge of tomorrow. At Dorchester Middle School we are inclusive and a school for all in our community. We aim to meet the needs of all our pupils whatever it takes.
We are proud to welcome visitors into our school and if you would like to see exactly how Dorchester Middle School ROARS, please contact our main office to arrange a visit.
Latest News
Congratulations Mr.Webb! What a beautiful couple and day to celebrate getting married!
The whole video we hope!
All the best to our leavers! Onwards and upwards!
A HUGE well done to Rebekah for raising so much money for the Little princess Trust! You may remember she had very very very long hair, which was cut off to help make wigs for others going through medical treatment. Well done Rebekah- we are so proud of you for making such a big difference!
Please ACT NOW. Everyone must re-apply, there are no exceptions. You will need to have your application submitted and approved by FRIDAY 21ST AUGUST to be able to order a FREE school meal with Local Food Links for when your child returns to school in September. You can scan the QR code below or use this link https://www.dorsetcouncil.gov.uk/w/free-school-meals?p_l_back_url=%2Fsearch%3Fq%3Dwhen%2Bcan%2Bi%2Bapply%2Bfor%2Bfree%2Bschool%2Bmeals%2Bfor%2B2026-2027
A VERY BIG thank you to all who made and bought cakes yesterday! We raised a very healthy £228.24 towards the 'Mission Jensen' Charity! Thank you to the Student council members for organising!
Pictures from last night- Year 8 Leavers assembly. Many moving and emotional moments as we say farewell to some wonderful pupils who have journeyed with us for these past four years. Special times have passed, memories made and exciting times lay ahead for them all!
We are so proud of our Eco club heroes! The year 7 eco heroes received a card and thank you for running the 'plates for change ' assembly for action against hunger and for donating money to the cause. They have worked so hard at this and have made a real difference!! Well done for being so ROARSOME!
Such a busy day at DMS- part six! Thank you to all our wonderful parents and supporters of our Cake Bake sale! They went down a storm! Mrs King worries there won't be enough cakes each time, but thankfully you all show up with your generosity of time and effort in producing some amazing cakes for us to sell! This cake sale was a special one... raising money for 'Mission Jensen' charity. As you can see- pupils came and snapped up so many yummy treats! We will update with the total we raised later on.
Such a busy day at DMS - Part Five New to this year, our lovely Miss Sales asked the Year Eight children to vote for specific teachers an alternative awards ceremony. Apologies for the poor quality pictures as everyone got their certificates really quickly. Also, where it was so hot my camera overheated and refused to work so not all the recipients are here. So sorry!

Wraparound Childcare
At Dorchester Middle School we run Wraparound Childcare which is a paid provision available to all. The childcare is available to parents during term time and is provided by our fantastic Wraparound Care Staff. This means children can arrive early from 7:30am and can stay after school until 5:30pm. During these sessions, children are offered a healthy breakfast or snacks, and a choice of fun activities, such as:
Homework Support
Board Games
Film night
Outside Activities (weather permitting)
Timings
Costing and Bookings
To cover the cost of the food, staff and activities, a fee will apply for these sessions. Payment is required in advance. Payments and bookings can be made via the ARBOR App for iPhone or ARBOR App for Android.
As an example, one child attending wraparound care for three hours every day for a month would cost £340.
If your child already attends Wraparound childcare, and you would like to contact the team, the phone number is: 07395075202. This phone line is open between 7.30 - 8.30am and 15.30 - 17.30pm. Please do inform us if you are running late or if your child won't be attending.
Help With Childcare Costs
You may be able to get help paying for childcare. You can check what support you could receive by using the official government Childcare Calculator: https://www.tax.service.gov.uk/childcare-calc/
Here are some of the main ways families may receive help:
Universal Credit Families receiving Universal Credit can claim back up to 85% of childcare costs. From April 2026, the maximum monthly claim will be £1,071.09 for one child and £1,836.16 for two or more children.
Tax‑Free Childcare For every £8 parents pay, the UK government adds £2. This can give up to £2,000 per child per year, or £4,000 if the child is disabled.
Childcare Vouchers These closed to new applicants in 2018, but parents already using them may continue if they are still with the same employer.
If you have any questions you can email: Mrs Nikki King at nking@dms.wessex.ac, but please be mindful that Mrs King would not be checking emails until the end of the school day (3:30pm).

Personal Development
Personal Development at Dorchester Middle School
At Dorchester Middle School, personal development is a cornerstone of our educational philosophy. We believe that nurturing the whole child is essential for their growth into kind, respectful, and resilient young people, ready to face the world with confidence and empathy.
A Holistic Approach to Learning
Personal development at Dorchester Middle School is not something that can be assessed on a termly basis. Instead, it is a continuous journey that we foster through a supportive and inclusive environment. Our dedicated staff work tirelessly to create opportunities for students to explore their interests, develop their strengths, and overcome challenges.
Key Aspects of Personal Development
Programs and Activities
Our personal development offer is designed to be engaging and impactful. From Pupil leadership opportunities and community service projects to mindfulness sessions and extracurricular clubs and visits. We provide a wide range of activities that support the growth of our pupils.
Preparing for the Future
By focusing on personal development, we prepare our pupils not just for academic success, but for life beyond school. We aim to develop well-rounded individuals who are ready to contribute positively to society and to lead fulfilling lives.
Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural aspect of learning at DMS
At our school, we offer a diverse range of assemblies designed to engage and educate our pupils. We invite a wide variety of speakers, including local ministers who provide valuable insights and guidance, and road safety experts who emphasise the importance of staying safe on the streets. Mental health ambassadors share strategies for maintaining well-being, while anti-bullying assemblies foster a supportive and inclusive environment. Our assemblies also feature exciting house competitions, spelling bees, and maths quizzes that encourage friendly rivalry and academic excellence. Additionally, we host members of the armed forces who inspire with their stories of service, and careers days that help students explore future opportunities.
Moreover, our assemblies play a crucial role in promoting the spiritual, moral, social, and cultural (SMSC) aspects of learning. Through these sessions, students are encouraged to reflect on their values, develop a sense of empathy, and appreciate diverse perspectives. This holistic approach ensures that our students grow not only academically but also as well-rounded individuals who are prepared to contribute positively to society.
At Dorchester Middle School, we are committed to helping each child grow into the best version of themselves. Join us in this journey of personal development and watch your child flourish.

SEND
Welcome to the SEND section of our website
Dorchester Middle School prides itself on its ability to offer and successfully deliver a full curriculum that is inclusive of all children, irrespective of need. The SEND department works to identify and celebrate individuals, ensure outreach support and specialist intervention is in place and support all staff members in providing equal opportunity to children with a wide range of academic, physical and mental health needs. As a result, the school is suitably equipped to deal with a wide range of individual needs. The school and the governing body regularly review its provision for children with special needs and ensure that its staff are well-prepared and trained.
For the majority of pupils, their needs will be met by our provision of a well-balanced, carefully planned and scaffolded curriculum in which skilled and diverse teaching strategies are employed. Some pupils will require some degree of extra support in their learning for varying periods of time, according to their level of need.
We recognise that some pupils will need more specialist and targeted support to engage fully in school life and meet their full potential if they are experiencing emotional or mental health difficulties, or have a specific learning difficulty or physical disability. These pupils will have a Individual Learning Plan and identified targets, strategies and provisions to support them.
At Dorchester Middle School, children are provided with the right support that is tailored to suit their needs, age and individual learning styles. For more detailed information about how we support children with SEND, please refer to the SEN Information Report.
The school maintains very close working relationships with children, staff, parents and other agencies and considers our partnership with parents to be of the utmost importance. We encourage parents to discuss progress regularly with teachers by attending all parents’ evenings. If you would like to discuss any issue regarding your child and Special Educational Needs and Disability, please, in the first instance, make an appointment to speak with your child’s home base tutor or, in the case that the concern lies within a particular subject, the subject teacher. Both will be happy to provide both information and support.
Below you will find a number of resources that we hope will help you.

Our pupils engage with a broad range of subjects, taught by passionate teachers through well‑designed and carefully sequenced schemes of learning tailored to meet their needs.
Our curriculum is underpinned by our ROARS values: Ready • Original • Ambitious • Respectful • Safe
These values guide every aspect of school life and shape the way our pupils learn, behave and engage with the wider world.
